native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber's relative signal is highest in the 4th millennium BCE (the millennium spanning 4000-3001 BCE), where all ten 100-year bins carry z = +1.46 to +1.54 (mean z = +1.48 versus a standardised mean of 0.00, SD 1.00 for the whole 4300-500 BCE frame), and it peaked over the interval 3300-3000 BCE, where four consecutive bins are tied at the series maximum of z = +1.54, inside a broader sharply bounded highstand of z >= +1.46 from 4000 to 3000 BCE. The next-highest value anywhere else in the record is only +0.37, so the winning and runner-up millennia (mean z = -0.15) do not overlap in value. Culturally the peak falls entirely within the Middle Neolithic (MN, 3400-3000 BCE; mean z = +1.52, highest of six periods), the highstand begins in the Early Neolithic, and it terminates abruptly at the MN -> Single Grave transition (+1.54 at 3000 BCE to +0.37 at 2900 BCE), after which amber never again exceeds +0.37 in 2400 years. Amber's importance was therefore a specifically Early/Middle Neolithic phenomenon culminating in the middle centuries of the 4th millennium BCE, not a feature of later metallurgical exchange networks.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Read capital.csv with decimal=','; derived CE=-BCE, calBP=1950+BCE. 2) Verified primary series capital.csv Zamber (39 bins, BCE 4300-500, 100-yr step, 0 NaN, mean 0.0008/sd 1.0014 = standardised within frame). 3) Cross-checked against time_series_data.csv: 37 overlapping century bins, max |Zamber-Amber| = 0.00e+00 -> identical units, no rescaling; Amber only 37/3601 non-null and all on the 100-yr grid; Amber_inter proven to be exactly a linear interpolation of Amber (max abs diff 2.22e-16), so used only as a rolling-window sensitivity. 4) Aggregated mean/max z per calendar millennium under THREE deliberately non-identical labelling conventions (S1 ordinal 4th=4000-3001; S2 rounded 4th=3999-3000; S3 3000-2000=4th) and reported all three. 5) Robustness: leave-one-bin-out over all 39 bins (winner never changes, 0/39 flips). 6) Peak defined as (a) tied-maximum bin set, (b) z>=1.46 highstand, (c) 300/500/1000-yr centred rolling means on Amber_inter. 7) Mapped peak/highstand onto capital.csv cultural periods EN/MN/SG/LN/OBA/YBA. 8) Pollen openness file used as context only (no amber column); amber-openness r reported at both annual (pseudoreplicated, -0.61) and 100-yr-bin (honest df, -0.52) resolution. 9) All tables written to out/, full stdout in out/analysis_log.txt.
